# The Pour-Over of Grace

## Scripture

"Being confident of this, that he who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus." — Philippians 1:6

## Reflection

Pour-over coffee teaches us something about how God works. You can't rush it. The water must be poured slowly, in stages, each pass blooming the grounds and drawing out flavor that only patience releases. Skip the pauses, dump the whole kettle at once, and you get a bitter, hollow cup. The process itself is the point.

So it is with grace. We want God's work in us finished by Monday—character polished, habits fixed, fruit ripened overnight. But the Lord, like a careful barista, pours in stages. He lets the grounds bloom. He waits while the extraction happens slowly, invisibly, in the hidden places. Philippians 1:6 doesn't say God *started* a good work; it says He will *carry it on to completion*. That means the awkward middle—the waiting, the slow drip of sanctification—is not evidence He has forgotten you. It is evidence He is still brewing.

The aroma rising from your kitchen isn't the finished cup, but it is the promise of one. Likewise, the small, imperfect changes in you now are the first fragrance of a work God will finish. So don't despise the slow pour. Don't bail on the process because the cup isn't full yet. The One who began it is faithful, and He does not abandon a batch halfway through.

## Prayer

Father, thank You for Your patient work in us. When we grow impatient with the slow pour of sanctification, remind us that You finish what You start. Teach us to trust Your timing and to rest in Your faithfulness. In Jesus' name, amen.

## One-Line Application

Trust the slow pour—God finishes what He begins in you.
